topic: Advanced Prototyping, Motion, and Interaction Design
learningObjectives: Design realistic interactive prototypes for complex user flows.
Use motion and transitions to communicate interface state changes.
Evaluate whether animation improves usability or introduces distraction.

activities.title: Advanced Prototype Architecture
activities.instruction: Connect triggers, states, transitions, and outcomes into a complete prototype flow.

content.concept: Advanced prototypes model multiple states, conditional paths, overlays, transitions, and interaction outcomes.
content.tip: Think of the prototype as a state machine: an action should move the interface from one understandable state to another.

activities.title: Motion Purpose Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each animation with the purpose it communicates.

content.concept: Motion can communicate hierarchy, continuity, feedback, progress, and changes between interface states.
content.tip: Ask what information the animation communicates rather than whether it simply looks attractive.

pairs.prompt: A button briefly changes state after being clicked.
A card smoothly moves into a new position after filtering.
A progress indicator animates while a file is uploading.
A modal smoothly appears above the current page.
A subtle animation draws attention to an important newly available action.

activities.title: Transition Timing Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust transition timing and observe how it affects perceived responsiveness.

content.concept: Animation timing affects perceived responsiveness, continuity, and the amount of attention an interaction requires.
content.tip: Compare very fast, balanced, and slow transitions to understand when motion becomes distracting.

scenarios.description: Moderate transition that provides visible continuity.
Long transition that may make simple interactions feel slow.

activities.title: Interaction State Builder
activities.instruction: Build a complete interaction from trigger to final state.

content.concept: A robust interaction defines the trigger, transition, system response, feedback, and resulting state.
content.tip: Every interaction should communicate what happened and what state the interface is now in.

separation.learning: Teach the concept through an interactive experience.
separation.assessment: Stored separately and completed after learning.
separation.practical: Stored separately and completed after assessment.
